# Cluely Review: Issues, Failures and Why It Falls Short

We reviewed Cluely AI in 2026, breaking down its real latency, accuracy failures, detection risks, and the honest case against using it in a live interview.

Cluely AI is a real-time interview assistance tool that overlays AI-generated answers on your screen during live job interviews without being detected by screen-sharing software. It launched in early 2025 and grew viral after a public demonstration went wrong, putting the company name all over tech media. But viral attention is not the same as a reliable product. In 2026, independent tests, Business Insider investigations, and real user reviews have surfaced serious problems with Cluely's latency, answer accuracy, fabrication risk, and long-term viability. This review covers every major failure point so you can make an informed decision before your next interview.

**Quick Summary: Cluely's Biggest Problems**

- Cluely advertises ~300ms response time, but independent tests measured 5 to 10 seconds under real interview pressure.
- A Business Insider test found Cluely fabricated work experience that was not on the user's resume, inventing roles and accomplishments that could get you caught in a follow-up question.
- Multiple reviewers question whether Cluely is durable at all, noting that ChatGPT, Granola, and other tools could make it irrelevant overnight.
- Detection risk is real: proctored assessments and AI behavior monitoring are already catching patterns linked to tools like Cluely.
- If you want genuine interview preparation that builds skills (and that you can actually defend in an interview), [AI mock interview tools](https://www.finalroundai.com/ai-mock-interview) like Final Round AI are a more defensible choice.

## What Is Cluely AI and How Does It Work?

Cluely AI is a screen overlay tool designed to listen to your job interview in real time, transcribe the interviewer's questions, and generate suggested answers that only you can see. The overlay is engineered to be invisible to standard screen-recording software and video call detection, including Zoom and Google Meet. The company positions it as a "cheating tool" rebranded as an AI assistant, and that framing is both its biggest marketing hook and its biggest liability.

The core setup is straightforward: connect your audio, optionally upload a resume, and Cluely listens to your interview and surfaces answers in a floating panel. The product attracted significant attention after founder Roy Lee wore it during a live investor pitch and on a date, turning the concept into a media story rather than just a product launch.

That viral moment drove search volume. It did not fix the product's underlying problems. If you want a full feature and pricing breakdown, our [Cluely AI review](https://www.finalroundai.com/blog/cluely-review-pros-cons) covers that in detail. This post focuses specifically on where the product fails.

## Cluely's Latency Problem: 300ms Claim vs. Reality

Cluely's marketing emphasizes near-instant response time, advertising approximately 300 milliseconds from question to generated answer. That number is not what independent testers have found.

Under real interview conditions, including the natural pauses, crosstalk, and audio variability of an actual video call, independent tests have measured response times of 5 to 10 seconds. That gap matters enormously in a live interview context. A 300ms delay is imperceptible. A 5-second delay means you are visibly pausing, looking at your screen, and waiting for an answer while the interviewer watches. That behavior is exactly what behavioral monitoring tools and attentive interviewers are trained to spot.

The discrepancy between advertised and real-world latency appears to come from testing conditions. Cluely's benchmark numbers likely reflect clean audio, fast internet, and simple questions. Real interviews have background noise, accents, incomplete sentences, and follow-up questions that compound the processing delay.

## Cluely's Accuracy Problem: Fabricated Answers and Invented Experience

This is the most serious failure Cluely has documented in external testing. In a Business Insider evaluation, Cluely fabricated work experience that was not on the user's resume. The tool invented job roles and accomplishments that the person had never held or done.

This is not a minor inaccuracy. It is a direct liability in an interview. If Cluely tells you to claim experience you do not have, and the interviewer follows up with a specific question about that experience, you are caught. The interviewer will not know you used an AI tool. They will know you lied. That ends the interview and potentially flags your profile with the company permanently.

The accuracy failure stems from how Cluely generates answers. When resume context is thin or the question does not match anything in the uploaded document, the model fills the gap with plausible-sounding but invented content. That is a known hallucination behavior in large language models. Cluely has not solved it, and in an interview setting, hallucinated answers carry real consequences.

## Cluely's Detection Risk: Is It Actually Undetectable?

Cluely claims its overlay is invisible to Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and HackerRank screen detection. That claim is accurate in a narrow technical sense. Standard screen-capture APIs cannot see the overlay window. But detection is not purely a technical question.

The actual risks that can get you caught include:

- **Behavioral monitoring:** A growing number of companies use AI-powered interview monitoring tools (HireVue, Canditech, and similar platforms) that analyze eye movement, gaze direction, and typing patterns. Looking at a second screen or a floating overlay produces gaze anomalies that these systems flag.
- **Follow-up questions:** Any interviewer who asks a specific follow-up question about an answer Cluely generated (especially a fabricated one) exposes the tool immediately. The answer does not match your actual knowledge.
- **Audio delays and unnatural phrasing:** Cluely's generated answers are written text that you are reading aloud. Experienced interviewers notice when answers sound scripted, when pauses precede full paragraphs, and when phrasing does not match conversational patterns.
- **Proctored assessments:** Technical interviews on platforms like CoderPad, Codility, and HackerRank with active proctoring flag multiple concurrent applications, unusual audio patterns, and mouse behavior anomalies.

Cluely being "screen-share undetectable" is one layer of a multi-layer detection environment. Passing the technical screen-capture test does not mean you are safe.

## Cluely's Viability Problem: A Feature, Not a Product

Beyond the accuracy and latency failures, the most damaging long-term criticism of Cluely is structural. Multiple independent reviewers, including venture-funded product analysts, have raised the question of whether Cluely is building a defensible product or a feature that platforms like ChatGPT, Granola, or native OS-level AI integrations will absorb within 12 to 18 months.

Apple Intelligence and Windows Copilot are both building screen-overlay AI assistance at the operating system level. Google's Gemini integration with Meet already surfaces meeting context in real time. The technical capability Cluely monetizes is becoming a commodity feature in tools people already pay for. When that happens, a standalone subscription to Cluely has no defensible reason to exist.

This is not a hypothetical risk. It is the same pattern that ended dozens of browser extension and screen-capture startups when browsers natively absorbed their functionality. For a tool that already has serious accuracy and latency problems, the long-term viability question makes the decision to pay for it even harder to justify.

## Cluely Pros: What Does Work

To give a balanced review, here is what Cluely does reasonably well:

- **Screen-share invisibility:** The overlay genuinely does not appear in standard Zoom, Meet, or Teams screen captures. That specific technical claim is accurate.
- **Simple setup:** Getting Cluely running takes less than 5 minutes. Resume upload, job URL paste, and you are live. The onboarding friction is low.
- **Behavioral question scaffolding:** For simple behavioral questions ("Tell me about yourself", "Why do you want this role?"), Cluely's generated structures are reasonable starting points when they do not hallucinate.
- **Awareness effect:** Some users report that having the overlay visible reduces interview anxiety, even when they do not read the answers directly. The psychological effect of a backup is real, even if the backup itself is unreliable.

## Cluely Cons: The Full List of Problems

- **5 to 10 second real-world latency** vs. the advertised 300ms, making it visible to interviewers in live settings.
- **Answer fabrication:** The tool invents experience and accomplishments not in your resume, creating direct liability if follow-up questions expose the lie.
- **No mock interview mode:** Cluely only works during live interviews. It cannot help you prepare, practice, or build actual skills before the interview. You need a separate AI mock interview tool for preparation.
- **Behavioral monitoring blind spots:** Eye tracking, gaze analysis, and audio pattern detection by interview platforms are not addressed by screen-capture invisibility.
- **Thin answer depth:** Responses tend toward brief bullet structures rather than the full Situation-Task-Action-Result narratives that senior-level behavioral interviewers expect.
- **Long-term product risk:** Native OS AI integrations from Apple, Google, and Microsoft are building the same capability into tools people already use and pay for.
- **No performance feedback:** After the interview, Cluely produces no coaching, no scoring, and no analysis of what you could improve. It is a live crutch with no learning loop.
- **Ethical and employment risk:** Using Cluely violates the terms of service of most interview platforms and most companies' hiring policies. Getting caught does not just end the interview; it can result in permanent blacklisting and in some cases professional reputation damage.

## Does Cluely Work? The Honest Answer

Cluely works in the narrow technical sense: it overlays AI-generated text on your screen during a video call without being captured by standard screen-share detection. That is what the product does.

Whether it works as an interview strategy is a different question. The combination of 5 to 10 second delays, answer fabrication, behavioral detection risk, and scripted answer delivery creates more failure modes than it removes. An interviewer who asks one follow-up question about an invented accomplishment has more evidence against you than if you had stumbled on the answer yourself.

The candidates who actually pass competitive technical and behavioral interviews do so because they have practiced, built mental frameworks, and can handle follow-up questions under pressure. Cluely does not build any of those capabilities. It replaces the thinking with a text overlay that occasionally invents things about your career.

Final Round AI covers both sides of the interview equation. The [Interview Copilot](https://www.finalroundai.com/interview-copilot) gives you real-time AI assistance during your live interview, just like Cluely, but grounded in your actual resume and the specific role so the answers are defensible when a follow-up comes. On top of that, AI mock interview practice, STAR-method coaching, and company-specific prep mean you walk in having already rehearsed, not just hoping the overlay fires in time.

The key differences:

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are the main problems with Cluely AI?

Cluely has three compounding problems. First, real-world latency is 5 to 10 seconds under actual interview conditions, far from the advertised 300 milliseconds. Second, a Business Insider test found Cluely fabricated work experience that was not on the user's resume, inventing job roles and accomplishments that create direct liability if a follow-up question exposes them. Third, detection risk extends well beyond screen-share capture: behavioral monitoring tools analyze eye movement and gaze patterns, and experienced interviewers notice when answers sound scripted and are preceded by visible pauses.

### Does Cluely AI actually work?

In the narrow technical sense, yes. Cluely does overlay AI-generated text on your screen during a video call without appearing in standard screen-share detection. Whether it works as an interview strategy is a different question. The combination of 5 to 10 second delays, occasional answer fabrication, behavioral detection risk, and scripted delivery creates more failure modes than it solves. An interviewer who asks one follow-up question about an invented accomplishment has more evidence against you than if you had stumbled on the answer yourself.

### Is Cluely AI worth it in 2026?

For most candidates, no. The accuracy risk alone is a serious liability. If Cluely generates a fabricated accomplishment and you repeat it, any follow-up question from the interviewer exposes you. The latency problem makes it visible in live settings. And the long-term viability is uncertain as Apple Intelligence, Windows Copilot, and Google Gemini build the same overlay capability into tools users already pay for. A more defensible investment is time spent with an AI mock interview tool that builds actual fluency rather than a live script.

### Cluely AI vs Final Round AI: what is the difference?

Cluely only works during live interviews and has no preparation or practice mode. Its answers can include fabricated experience that does not match your resume. Final Round AI provides both live interview support through Interview Copilot, which is grounded in your actual resume, and a full practice environment through AI Mock Interview. The key difference is that Final Round AI gives you both the live safety net and the underlying skill to handle follow-up questions without needing the overlay to fire correctly.

### Why does Cluely AI have latency issues?

Cluely's advertised 300ms response time is measured under clean test conditions: clear audio, fast internet, and simple direct questions. Real interviews have background noise, accents, incomplete sentences, and follow-up questions that compound the processing delay. Under those conditions, independent tests measured 5 to 10 seconds between the interviewer finishing a question and Cluely surfacing a suggested answer. That delay is visible in a live video call and is exactly what attentive interviewers and behavioral monitoring tools are designed to catch.

Cluely has three problems that compound each other: the answers arrive too slowly to be invisible, they sometimes invent things you have to defend, and the detection environment has moved far beyond screen-capture checks. You are taking on real professional risk for a tool that may not even deliver accurate information when it does respond.

If you are preparing for competitive interviews, the better investment is time spent with a real AI mock interview tool that builds fluency, not a live script that breaks down the moment a follow-up question arrives.
